questions.stem: Why do gold-layer tables built for reporting often denormalize descriptive attributes into dimension tables?

options.text: So that the tables no longer need keys
So that every attribute is stored only once
So that storage use goes down
So that reports need fewer joins and are simpler to query

questions.explanation: Flattening related attributes into one dimension per subject gives a star schema that reporting tools query with few joins. It stores some values more than once, which is the accepted trade-off.

questions.stem: Product, Subcategory and Category are three normalized tables. For a star schema, what should the Product dimension look like?

options.text: The fact table carrying the category names, with no Product dimension
Three dimension tables, each joined to the fact table
A Category table with a list of products in one column
One Product table that also carries each product's subcategory and category names

questions.explanation: A star schema flattens a snowflaked hierarchy into one dimension, so each product row includes its subcategory and category and the fact table joins to one table.

questions.stem: While flattening Product with Category, some products have no category yet but must still appear in the dimension. Which join keeps them?

options.text: Inner join from Product to Category
Left outer join from Product to Category
Right outer join from Product to Category

questions.explanation: A left outer join keeps every product and leaves the category columns empty where there's no match; you can then fill them with a value such as Unknown. An inner join would drop those products.

questions.stem: Which two are costs of denormalizing data? Each correct answer is a complete solution.

options.text: A change to an attribute has to be applied to many rows
The data can no longer be stored as Delta
The same value is stored many times, using more storage

questions.explanation: Denormalized tables repeat values, so they take more space and an attribute change touches every row that repeats it. They need fewer joins, not more.
